paragraphs: Clustering with multiple views means grouping samples using several complementary descriptions of the same items. When some descriptions are missing, the method must infer relationships from incomplete evidence. Anchor-based approaches make this manageable at large scale by learning representative anchors. This paper identifies a problem: missing samples can distort those representatives, shifting the anchors and weakening the resulting clusters.

The proposed method uses reconstruction across views to reduce this distortion while recovering missing samples. It also changes the combinations used for reconstruction. Convex combinations restrict reconstructed points to the region enclosed by the anchors. Affine combinations allow reconstruction beyond that region, giving the method access to areas that the more restrictive approach cannot represent.

Experiments on four benchmark datasets and three large-scale datasets support the method's effectiveness. The contribution connects two issues that otherwise reinforce each other: biased representatives and restricted reconstruction. Improving how views inform one another addresses anchor learning, while expanding the reconstruction space helps recover samples in previously inaccessible regions.
neurips-2024-alleviate-anchor-shift-expl.tldr: Cross-view reconstruction reduces distorted anchors and reaches beyond their convex hull to improve clustering with missing views.

paragraphs: Meta-reinforcement learning trains an agent to adapt through experience stored in a sequence model's memory. This resembles the way a language model can use examples within its current context. Much existing meta-RL work studies small variations of one task, however. Expanding to many different tasks introduces optimization difficulties, particularly when training does not provide explicit task labels.

AMAGO-2 focuses on uneven return scales: tasks with differently sized rewards can produce imbalanced training losses. Building on Transformer-based meta-RL, the authors express both actor and critic objectives as classification terms. These are the objectives used to train the agent's behavior and evaluate it. The reformulation separates optimization from the current numerical scale of returns.

Large-scale comparisons cover Meta-World ML45, Multi-Game Procgen, Multi-Task POPGym, Multi-Game Atari, and BabyAI. The reported results show substantial progress on online adaptation across tasks and on memory problems without task labels. They support loss formulation as an important ingredient in scaling meta-RL beyond narrowly related tasks.
neurips-2024-amago-2-breaking-the-multi-.tldr: AMAGO-2 converts actor and critic objectives into classification terms to improve Transformer-based adaptation across unlabeled tasks.

paragraphs: Rotary position embedding, or RoPE, gives language models position information through rotations. Its base parameter is often adjusted when extending a model's context length. A common justification is that this adjustment reduces the mismatch between position embeddings encountered during training and those encountered in longer inputs.

The paper argues that this justification can produce only superficial long-context ability. The authors revisit RoPE's role and introduce a property called long-term decay. From this analysis, they derive an absolute lower bound on the base value needed for a specified context-length capability. The claim makes the base parameter a constraint on attainable context length, beyond its role in addressing unfamiliar position embeddings.

Both theoretical analysis and empirical evidence support the relationship between the base and context length. The distinction matters when interpreting an extended context window: reducing positional distribution mismatch does not by itself settle whether the model has the intended capability. The lower bound supplies a necessary base-value requirement; it does not establish that choosing a sufficiently large base alone guarantees successful long-context behavior.
neurips-2024-base-of-rope-bounds-context.tldr: The paper derives a lower bound on RoPE's base parameter for a given context-length capability and supports the relationship empirically.

paragraphs: Domain adaptation aims to maintain performance across different data domains. Some Bayesian approaches infer a hidden domain index when domain labels are unavailable, but assume those indices follow a single Gaussian distribution. This paper argues that such a prior overlooks structure among domains, treating their organization too simply.

GMDI replaces that single distribution with a Gaussian mixture over domain indices. A Chinese Restaurant Process adaptively determines how many mixture components are used in the domain-theme space. This lets the representation accommodate multiple groups of domains while adjusting the mixture structure during learning. The theoretical analysis shows a tighter evidence lower bound, meaning the variational bound lies closer to the log-likelihood.

The reported classification results outperform the compared approaches, exceeding VDI by up to 3.4% and reaching 99.3%. For regression, mean squared error falls by up to 21%, from 3.160 to 2.493. Together, these findings support modeling relationships among hidden domains more flexibly, with both a stronger variational bound and improved predictive results in the reported comparisons.
neurips-2024-bayesian-domain-adaptation-.tldr: GMDI adaptively models hidden domain indices with a Gaussian mixture, tightening the variational bound and improving reported adaptation results.

paragraphs: Cambrian-1 investigates multimodal language models by putting their visual components at the center of the study. The authors argue that progress in language modeling has not been matched by equally systematic exploration of visual representations. They use language models and visual instruction tuning to compare more than 15 vision models, including self-supervised, strongly supervised, and combined representations.

The work also examines how multimodal benchmarks are consolidated and interpreted. On the architecture side, it introduces the spatial vision aggregator, a connector that dynamically integrates visual features with a language model while accounting for spatial information and reducing token count. On the data side, it studies instruction-tuning data assembled from public sources and emphasizes balancing its distribution.

The resulting model family achieves reported state-of-the-art performance. Its broader contribution is an open collection of practical ingredients: weights, code, tools, datasets, and detailed training and evaluation recipes. These resources make the visual design choices and their evaluation part of the contribution, alongside the resulting models' benchmark performance.
neurips-2024-cambrian-1-a-fully-open-vis.tldr: Cambrian-1 combines a broad study of visual representations, a spatially aware connector, and open training resources for multimodal language models.

paragraphs: Imitation learning uses expert demonstrations when a reward signal or performance measure is not supplied. Difficulties arise when the learner and expert observe different information, or when hidden variables bias the demonstrations. Existing causal approaches can require knowledge of the underlying causal structure, which may be unavailable.

This paper studies these difficulties in Markov decision processes through partial identification. Instead of requiring the data to determine one unique account of the system, it considers settings where either the transition distribution or reward function remains non-identifiable. The authors first establish a general obstacle: with unobserved confounders, a learner generally cannot imitate expert performance.

They then develop two causal imitation algorithms by augmenting GAIL. In the partially identifiable settings analyzed, the algorithms can produce policies guaranteed to achieve expert performance. The significance is the separation between general impossibility and structured cases where successful imitation remains possible. The guarantees apply to those analyzed settings, rather than removing the confounding obstacle for every imitation problem.
neurips-2024-causal-imitation-for-markov.tldr: Two extensions of GAIL achieve expert-performance guarantees in analyzed partially identifiable settings despite confounded demonstrations.

paragraphs: Federated learning keeps client data local while sharing gradients for collaborative training. Those gradients can nevertheless reveal the underlying examples. Previous text reconstruction attacks were limited to approximate recovery of small batches and short sequences. DAGER is presented as an algorithm capable of exactly recovering entire batches of input text.

The method combines two properties: self-attention gradients have a low-rank structure, and token embeddings come from a discrete set. Together, these enable a check for whether a candidate token sequence belongs to the client data. DAGER uses an exhaustive heuristic search for encoder architectures and a greedy approach for decoder architectures. Its setting assumes an honest-but-curious server and requires no prior information about the data.

A GPU implementation experimentally recovers batches of up to 128 examples. Reported comparisons show 20-fold higher speed at the same batch size, support for batches ten times larger, and ROUGE-1/2 above 0.99. These findings demonstrate substantial text leakage through shared gradients under the studied setting, despite keeping the original examples on clients.
neurips-2024-dager-exact-gradient-invers.tldr: DAGER exploits self-attention gradient structure and discrete token embeddings to recover full text batches from shared gradients.

paragraphs: Reconstructing a three-dimensional head from one image requires matching the visible appearance while producing realistic views from other directions. GAN inversion approaches this by mapping the image into a generative model's latent space. Existing encoders are largely built on EG3D, whose emphasis on near-frontal images limits its ability to synthesize comprehensive views.

This paper instead builds on PanoHead, which supports synthesis around a full 360-degree perspective. It introduces two encoders specialized for faithful reconstruction and realistic generation from different viewpoints. A stitching framework combines their predictions in the triplane representation. The aim is to retain the strengths of both encoders within a single reconstructed head.

Combining specialized predictions requires consistency where they are stitched together. The authors train the encoders with tailored losses, including an adversarial loss from an occlusion-aware triplane discriminator. Experiments report qualitative and quantitative improvements over existing encoder training methods. The results support coordinating reconstruction fidelity and viewpoint realism through specialized encoders whose internal representations are trained to fit together.
neurips-2024-dual-encoder-gan-inversion-.tldr: Two coordinated encoders and triplane stitching improve single-image head reconstruction and realistic synthesis across viewpoints.

paragraphs: Low-bit quantization represents a language model's numerical values with fewer bits, but unusually large activations make that representation difficult. The paper distinguishes ordinary large activations from much more extreme massive outliers. Existing approaches mainly address the former and can lose substantial performance when the latter remain poorly controlled.

DuQuant redistributes these activations through a sequence of transformations. It first builds a rotation using known outlier dimensions and applies it within blocks, spreading outliers into neighboring channels. A zigzag permutation then balances the outlier distribution across blocks, reducing differences between them. A further rotation smooths the activations again before quantization.

The reported evaluations span multiple tasks and language models of different types and sizes. DuQuant outperforms the compared state-of-the-art methods, including when both weights and activations use four-bit quantization. The findings support addressing outliers at two levels: their concentration within a block and their uneven distribution across blocks. This provides a concrete explanation for why the combination of rotations and permutation improves the quantized models.
neurips-2024-duquant-distributing-outlie.tldr: DuQuant combines block rotations and a balancing permutation to redistribute activation outliers and improve low-bit language models.

paragraphs: Generating images at different resolutions and aspect ratios requires a model to handle changing image dimensions without losing visual quality. The paper identifies two difficulties with existing Transformer-based diffusion approaches: quadratic computational cost and limited ability to extrapolate to other resolutions. FlowDCN explores a purely convolutional architecture for this problem.

Its central component is a learnable group-wise deformable convolution block. This provides the flexibility used to handle different resolutions within one model. The proposed architecture has linear time and memory complexity, making its computational scaling a central part of the contribution alongside image quality and resolution flexibility.

On the 256-by-256 ImageNet benchmark, FlowDCN achieves a reported state-of-the-art sFID of 4.30 and comparable resolution extrapolation results. Against the Transformer-based counterparts studied, it converges using one-fifth as many images, reduces parameters by 8%, and reduces FLOPs by 20%, while improving visual quality. These comparisons support convolutional generative models as a promising route to efficient image synthesis across varying resolutions.
neurips-2024-exploring-dcn-like-architec.tldr: FlowDCN uses deformable convolutions for flexible-resolution image generation with linear time and memory complexity and strong reported efficiency.

paragraphs: Training agents in games or robotics requires simulations that implement the intended task. Generating these from language is broader than writing a reward function or selecting task settings. FactorSim tackles the full simulation: it produces code from language input that can then be used to train an agent.

The method takes advantage of the modular structure of coded simulations. It uses a factored partially observable Markov decision process representation to reduce how much context each generation step depends on. Breaking the simulation into factors gives the generation process a structure aligned with the components of the environment being constructed.

The authors also introduce a benchmark that evaluates whether generated code matches the prompt and whether the resulting simulations support zero-shot transfer in reinforcement learning. FactorSim outperforms existing methods on prompt alignment, transfer ability, and human evaluation, and is demonstrated on robotic tasks. These findings assess the generated environments both as implementations of instructions and as training resources whose usefulness extends to agent behavior.
neurips-2024-factorsim-generative-simula.tldr: FactorSim generates complete simulation code from language using a factored representation that reduces context dependence during generation.

paragraphs: Cox proportional hazards models are widely used in survival analysis because they combine interpretability, flexibility, and predictive performance. Training becomes difficult with many observations, many features, or strongly correlated features. The paper traces a problem in Newton-based algorithms to second-order derivatives that become very small away from the region near the minimizer.

The authors develop alternative optimization methods by constructing surrogate functions that exploit mathematical structure in the Cox model. Training proceeds by minimizing these surrogates. The proposed methods are described as easy to implement and come with guarantees of monotonic loss decrease and global convergence, addressing the convergence difficulty identified in the existing approach.

Experiments support the methods' computational efficiency. The paper also applies them to Cox models with a cardinality constraint, which limits how many features can be selected. This makes very sparse, high-quality models practical to construct in the reported work. The contribution therefore links better optimization to a modeling capability: fitting useful survival models under an explicit restriction on feature count.
neurips-2024-fastsurvival-hidden-computa.tldr: FastSurvival exploits Cox-model structure to obtain convergent optimization methods and make very sparse survival models practical.

paragraphs: This paper asks how architecture affects the basic capabilities acquired during language-model pretraining. These include language modeling within and outside the training distribution, transfer learning, and few-shot learning. Its starting point is a decline in these capabilities in Transformers with wider feed-forward networks, shifting attention from model scale to how computation is organized.

The authors identify the relative contribution of multi-head attention as a key factor. They describe attention as a combination function and find that widening feed-forward networks reduces its contribution to pretrained language modeling. Experiments support this explanation. They then propose Combination Enhanced Architecture, or CEA, to address the associated loss of capability.

The analysis and architectural change are also extended to mixture-of-experts Transformers. On a model with 14 billion parameters, CEA produces significant reported improvements in base capabilities. The result gives the explanation practical relevance beyond the initial architecture studied: the balance of attention's contribution can help guide changes to both wider feed-forward models and mixture-of-experts models.
neurips-2024-how-does-architecture-influ.tldr: The paper links weakened base capabilities to attention's reduced contribution and proposes CEA to improve wider-feed-forward and MoE Transformers.

paragraphs: Representations of instructions are useful for selecting training data and retrieving demonstrations. Ordinary text embeddings capture broad semantic content, which can interfere with identifying the kind of task an instruction requests. This paper emphasizes task identity as the relevant organizing principle for such instruction-related uses.

The authors introduce instruction embeddings and create the Instruction Embedding Benchmark for training and evaluation. They also propose Prompt-based Instruction Embedding, or PIE, as a baseline designed to make representations focus more strongly on tasks. The distinction is between representing the overall content of an instruction and representing the operation it asks a model to perform.

PIE is compared with other embedding methods on two tasks in the new benchmark and performs better at identifying task categories. Applications across four downstream tasks also support the usefulness of instruction embeddings. The results connect the proposed representation goal to practical uses: when selecting or retrieving instructions, accurately capturing task type can provide information that broad semantic similarity does not adequately isolate.
neurips-2024-instruction-embedding-laten.tldr: Instruction embeddings focus on requested task types, with PIE improving task identification and supporting four downstream applications.

paragraphs: Agents trained together through multi-agent reinforcement learning can invent communication protocols that help them cooperate. Those protocols are often difficult for humans or separately trained agents to interpret. This creates a barrier to ad-hoc teamwork, where participants cannot depend on having learned the same private communication system together.

The proposed pipeline aligns the agents' communication space with an embedding space for human natural language. It grounds their messages using synthetic data generated by embodied language models in interactive teamwork scenarios. Human-language representations thereby provide a shared reference for communication that would otherwise emerge solely from joint reinforcement learning.

The reported results show that language grounding preserves task performance while speeding the emergence of communication. The learned protocols also generalize without additional training to teamwork with unseen teammates and unfamiliar task states. These findings support language grounding as a way to make coordination less dependent on a fixed training group. The work presents this as progress toward collaboration between artificial agents and humans, rather than reporting universal real-world teamwork capability.
neurips-2024-language-grounded-multi-age.tldr: Grounding agent communication in natural-language embeddings preserves performance and enables reported zero-shot teamwork with unfamiliar partners and states.

paragraphs: Diffusion models can serve as priors in Bayesian inverse problems, helping represent the underlying data that noisy or incomplete measurements came from. Training these models usually requires many clean examples. That requirement becomes a practical obstacle when the available dataset itself consists of degraded observations.

The paper proposes training diffusion models using only incomplete and noisy observations through expectation maximization. This connects learning the model with inference about the unobserved clean data. The method also includes an improved posterior sampling scheme for unconditional diffusion models, providing a sampling component within the proposed learning approach.

A central claim is that the procedure produces proper diffusion models, a property the authors identify as crucial for downstream tasks and distinguish from previous approaches. The paper supplies empirical evidence for its effectiveness. Its contribution is therefore a route from degraded training observations to a diffusion prior that can be used subsequently, reducing dependence on access to a separate collection of clean training examples.
neurips-2024-learning-diffusion-priors-f.tldr: An expectation-maximization approach trains proper diffusion models directly from noisy, incomplete observations and includes improved posterior sampling.

paragraphs: Language-model compression aims to reduce the computation and storage needed for deployment. Many techniques have been proposed, but evaluating each on a narrow selection of models, datasets, or metrics makes it difficult to decide which approach fits a particular use case. LLMCBench addresses this comparison problem with a broader evaluation framework.

The authors begin by analyzing requirements from actual model production. They use those requirements to design evaluation tracks and metrics, then conduct extensive comparisons of several mainstream compression approaches. This ties the benchmark's organization to deployment needs rather than treating compression quality as a single undifferentiated outcome.

The work also analyzes the experimental results to provide insights for compression design. Its stated contribution is a systematic basis for understanding choices across scenarios and informing future algorithms. The practical value lies in connecting requirements, measurement, and comparison: a deployment decision becomes easier to assess when methods are evaluated within a framework built around the demands they are meant to satisfy.
neurips-2024-llmcbench-benchmarking-larg.tldr: LLMCBench compares mainstream language-model compression methods using evaluation tracks and metrics informed by production requirements.

paragraphs: Medical language-model benchmarks often concentrate on answering questions or passing exams. MedJourney broadens the evaluation target to the support a patient may need throughout a hospital visit. It organizes that journey into four stages: planning, access, delivery, and ongoing care, with multiple tasks assigned to each stage.

The benchmark contains 12 datasets. Five are newly introduced, while seven are constructed from existing datasets. This organization brings distinct stages of patient support into one evaluation framework, allowing model assessment to follow the clinical journey rather than focus only on isolated medical knowledge questions.

The authors evaluate three categories of models: proprietary services such as GPT-4, public models such as QWen, and specialized medical models such as HuatuoGPT2. The contribution is both the benchmark and this cross-category evaluation. Its stated purpose is to clarify model performance across patient-facing clinical tasks and inform practical healthcare applications. The abstract presents this broader assessment framework without naming a winning model or establishing clinical deployment outcomes.
neurips-2024-medjourney-benchmark-and-ev.tldr: MedJourney evaluates language models across four stages of a patient's clinical journey using 12 datasets.

paragraphs: Safety defenses can make language models more likely to refuse instructions, including benign requests that could receive useful answers. The authors identify this rejection-oriented behavior as a usability problem. MoGU aims to improve responses to malicious instructions while preserving helpful behavior on legitimate ones.

The framework creates two variants of a base language model: one focused on usability and another focused on safety. A dynamic router controls their relative contributions. For malicious instructions, it gives greater weight to the safe variant; for benign instructions, it favors the usable variant. This makes the balance between the two behaviors depend on the instruction being processed.

Comparisons with multiple defense strategies across open-source language models support MoGU's reported superiority. Additional analysis finds that the routing mechanism effectively balances the variants through its assigned weights. The authors release safer versions of Llama2, Vicuna, Falcon, Dolphin, and Baichuan2. The findings support dynamic weighting as a practical way to address the safety-usability tension in the evaluated models.
neurips-2024-mogu-a-framework-for-enhanc.tldr: MoGU dynamically weights safety-focused and usability-focused model variants to improve safety while retaining helpful responses.

paragraphs: PiMForce estimates pressure across the hand by combining two sources of information: three-dimensional hand posture and surface electromyography signals measured at the forearm. The posture supplies spatial information about the hand, while the muscle signals capture dynamic activity. The framework uses them together to handle varied hand-object interactions.

The authors also build a multimodal collection system consisting of a pressure glove, an electromyography armband, and markerless finger tracking. Using this system, they collect synchronized posture, muscle-signal, and pressure data from 21 participants. The dataset covers different hand postures and interaction scenarios, providing aligned measurements of the inputs and the pressure being estimated.

The paper reports precise, robust whole-hand pressure estimation in complex and natural interactions. It attributes the improvement over traditional approaches based on electromyography or vision to combining posture with muscle activity. The contribution includes both the estimation framework and the coordinated measurement dataset, making the relationship between hand configuration, muscular activity, and exerted pressure central to the approach.
neurips-2024-posture-informed-muscular-f.tldr: PiMForce combines 3D hand posture with forearm muscle signals to improve whole-hand pressure estimation across varied interactions.

paragraphs: The paper treats designing a molecule for two protein targets as a generative task. Dual-target therapies are motivated partly by their potential to overcome drug resistance. The authors curate a dataset of potential target pairs from synergistic drug combinations and ask how models trained on single-target protein-ligand complexes can support this new task.

Their method aligns two binding pockets in three-dimensional space using protein-ligand binding priors. It constructs two complex graphs that share the ligand nodes, allowing information from both targets to influence the same generated molecule. SE(3)-equivariant composed message passing combines these signals, respecting changes in spatial orientation and position, and produces a composed drift for both three-dimensional and categorical generation.

The approach transfers knowledge from single-target pretraining to dual-target generation in a zero-shot manner. The authors also adapt linker-design methods as strong comparison baselines. Extensive experiments support the proposed method's effectiveness against the evaluated alternatives. These results concern the generative design task; the therapeutic motivation supplies the reason for pursuing molecules that address two targets.
neurips-2024-reprogramming-pretrained-ta.tldr: The method composes pretrained single-target diffusion models to generate candidate dual-target molecules without dual-target retraining.

paragraphs: This paper studies whether information from the openly available Segment Anything Model can support adversarial attacks against models fine-tuned from it. The setting excludes access to downstream tasks and datasets, preventing the attacker from training a similar task-specific surrogate. The authors demonstrate that transferable vulnerabilities can still exist under these restrictions.

Their method, UMI-GRAT, combines universal meta-initialization with a gradient robust loss. Meta-initialization extracts vulnerabilities from the foundation model to guide perturbation generation. The theoretical analysis identifies a mismatch in attack update directions when directly maximizing distances between the original model's encoded features: gradients can differ after downstream fine-tuning.

The robust loss addresses that mismatch by using gradient-based noise augmentation to simulate the associated uncertainty. Experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the combined attack against SAM and its downstream models. The findings show that vulnerability inherited from a shared foundation can matter even when an attacker lacks downstream training information, and that accounting for gradient differences improves transfer in the reported evaluations.
neurips-2024-transferable-adversarial-at.tldr: UMI-GRAT improves attacks transferred from public SAM to downstream models without access to their tasks or datasets.

paragraphs: Three-dimensional medical image segmentation must use both details within individual slices and context across the full volume. Conventional methods often rely on isotropic 3D convolutions, despite differences in information density across imaging axes. The paper argues that this can leave useful features within axial slices insufficiently exploited.

The proposed U-shaped Connection, or uC, replaces standard skip connections with simplified 2D U-Nets. These connections strengthen extraction of features within the slice plane while the surrounding 3D convolutions retain volumetric context. The authors integrate this design into an enhanced 3D U-Net backbone called uC 3DU-Net.

Evaluation covers FLARE2021, OIMHS, FeTA2021, AbdomenCT-1K, and BTCV. Across the reported experiments, the method surpasses contemporary state-of-the-art models while reducing parameter count and computational complexity. The result supports a targeted combination of two-dimensional and three-dimensional processing: the added slice-level structure improves feature use without requiring a larger or more computationally expensive model in these comparisons.
neurips-2024-upping-the-game-how-2d-u-ne.tldr: Replacing 3D U-Net skip connections with simplified 2D U-Nets improves reported segmentation while reducing model size and computation.

paragraphs: 3D Gaussian Splatting reconstructs scene appearance and geometry, but its usual learning pipeline does not quantify uncertainty. This matters for applications such as robotic mapping and navigation, where knowing which parts of a representation are uncertain can be useful. The paper adds uncertainty estimation through a Bayesian framework.

The method constructs variational multi-scale Gaussians using explicit scale information in the representation. An offset table efficiently generates local samples by modifying selected attributes while sharing other base attributes. Variational inference learns this table under a multi-scale prior. The resulting posterior describes uncertainty in individual Gaussian components and supports predictive uncertainty during the forward pass.

Benchmark experiments report well-aligned uncertainty calibration and better rendering quality than previous uncertainty-aware view-synthesis methods. The estimated parameter uncertainty also enables automatic removal of noisy Gaussians, leaving a higher-fidelity portion of the reconstructed scene. This connects uncertainty estimation to a concrete use within reconstruction: identifying components whose removal improves the visual quality of the retained scene.
neurips-2024-variational-multi-scale-rep.tldr: A variational multi-scale representation estimates uncertainty in 3D Gaussian Splatting and uses it to improve rendering and remove noisy components.

paragraphs: Vision-language models involve choices about pretrained components, architecture, data, and training. The authors observe that these choices are often insufficiently justified, making it difficult to determine which decisions actually improve performance. Their study conducts extensive experiments across these areas to provide a firmer basis for building such models.

The findings are consolidated into Idefics2, an eight-billion-parameter foundational vision-language model. This makes the work both a study of design decisions and a concrete model built from the resulting evidence. The emphasis on multiple parts of the development process connects component selection and training choices to the performance of the completed system.

Idefics2 achieves reported state-of-the-art results within its size category across several multimodal benchmarks and often matches models four times larger. That comparison suggests the studied design choices can support strong performance at a smaller parameter count. The authors release base, instruction-tuned, and chat versions, together with datasets created for training, making the resulting model family and training resources available.
neurips-2024-what-matters-when-building-.tldr: A systematic study of vision-language design choices produces Idefics2, an eight-billion-parameter model that often matches much larger models.
